name: wireshark
desc: Network analyzer and capture tool - without graphical user interface
why: Command-line packet capture is a door into every protocol on the wire, though it is a famous default.

brief.what_it_is: Wireshark is a free, open-source network protocol analyzer. It captures live traffic from a computer's network interfaces and lets you browse it interactively, with deep inspection of hundreds of protocols. Its input is live traffic or existing capture files, and its output is decoded packet views, statistics, and exported or converted capture files. This Homebrew formula packages only the command-line side: tshark (terminal Wireshark), dumpcap (capture), capinfos, captype, editcap, mergecap, text2pcap, reordercap, rawshark, randpkt, dftest, idl2wrs, mmdbresolve, and sharkd. The homepage and the User's Guide describe the graphical app, which this formula does not install by default.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as 'The world's leading network protocol analyzer' for diagnosing networks and understanding traffic: finding bottlenecks, troubleshooting faster, and seeing what protocols are doing. The formula description frames it as a door into every protocol on the wire.
brief.how_it_works: The User's Guide's table of contents shows a capture layer (live capture with capture filters and capture file modes), a dissection layer that decodes protocols, and statistics and reassembly on top. Capture is done with dumpcap, and tshark gives the same dissection on the terminal. The fetched pages are only a table of contents and homepage copy, so the detailed mechanism is not confirmed here.

commands_seen.context: From the formula caveats, not the README: installs Wireshark.app (the GUI) via Homebrew Cask.
From the formula caveats, not the README: installs ChmodBPF so that capture interfaces appear on macOS, where the list is empty by default.

brief.install_notes: Homebrew's formula installs only the command-line utilities by default. For the GUI, run 'brew install wireshark-app'. On macOS, if the list of capture interfaces is empty (the default), install ChmodBPF with 'brew install --cask wireshark-chmodbpf'. The User's Guide's table of contents also has chapters on Windows installation with Npcap and on building from source under UNIX and Linux, but I did not read those pages.
brief.standout: Live capture and interactive dissection are the same engine as the GUI, and it runs in a terminal (tshark) or as a server (sharkd), so it fits scripts and headless boxes. The command-line package is a suite of small single-purpose tools for editing, merging, converting, and inspecting capture files.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage shows stable release 4.6.9, development release 4.7.4, and an old stable 4.4.19. Its news list is current, with an announcement dated 2026-10-06 and a SharkFest EU 2026 notice. Caveat: the User's Guide page says Version 5.1.0, which does not match the 4.6.9 stable release shown on the homepage. I did not check release dates or commit history.
brief.caveats: Licensed under GPL version 2, per the homepage FAQ. On macOS, capture needs ChmodBPF or a similar permission setup. The formula installs only the CLI tools by default. The homepage is heavy on marketing and membership content. The User's Guide version (5.1.0) and the stable release (4.6.9) on the homepage disagree, so check which version you are reading. The formula's scout note calls command-line capture 'a famous default', which is the brew-side framing and not the project's own.
quotes: The world's leading network protocol analyzer
Wireshark lets you dive deep into your network traffic - free and open source.

Comprehensive Network Analysis. Wireshark is a powerful, open-source network protocol analyzer that allows users to capture and interactively browse the traffic running on a computer network, providing deep inspection of hundreds of protocols.
